title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East (show b- Late?) on 1970-01-02
source: Soundboard > 7 1/2' Reel Master @ 7.5 ips (Recorded By Bear on a Sony 770 Reel Deck) > 1st gen (TDK SAX-100 cassette) from Dick Latvala (Master Reel Playback on a Technics 1506 Reel to Reel > Tascam 122 MK111 Cassette Deck No dolby) > Analog to Digital (Cassettes played back on Nakamichi Dragon > Sony PCM-R700 DAT @ 44.1 by Jim Wise 1998); Edited and mastered SIRMIck

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with TC front‑and‑center and solid mix, capturing a 1970 Fillmore show where Dark Star and Tighten Up shine despite some balance issues.
ai_review.review: The performance is an exploratory romp highlighted by an expansive Dark Star that many deem one of the best, plus a fiery Feelin' Groovy jam and a scorching Tighten Up sequence. The soundboard source is generally clear, though the mix pushes keyboards forward and makes Phil’s bass hard to hear at times.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical moments (Dark Star, Tighten Up) and note good soundboard quality, but a few criticize the Dark Star's minimalism and balance issues, leading to an overall strong yet not flawless rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear overall mix with Tom Constanten prominent; Bear handled faders. Bass (Phil) is buried for some listeners, but the recording retains good fidelity and minimal noise.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set opens with tight vocal harmonies, then drifts into exploratory jams; Dark Star serves as the centerpiece before a high‑energy Tighten Up finale, giving the show a free‑form, Fillmore vibe.

band_member_comments.Phil: His bass is difficult to hear in this mix, making his presence less audible.
band_member_comments.Bob: Praised for strong guitar work and a notable solo during the Tighten Up jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s keyboards are pushed forward in the mix, giving the show a distinctive keyboard‑heavy texture.
